harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as the DNS resolver for the shared 10.100.11.0/24 network using PowerDNS Recursor (service dns forwarding): listens on 10.100.11.10, allows queries from the /24, forwards to 1.1.1.1/9.9.9.9 upstream, and serves an authoritative A record for inventory.internal -> 10.100.11.11 (node2). node2 and node3 were reconfigured via nmcli (ipv4.dns=10.100.11.10, ipv4.ignore-auto-dns=yes) to resolve through node1. Verified inventory.internal resolves to node2's address and external names (google.com) resolve via upstream forwarding from both node2 and node3. Completed the mandatory sequential restart protocol on all three nodes: captured pre-restart boot_id/service baselines, rebooted one node at a time via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified DNS config/resolution after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected all three nodes' OS, IPs, and cluster network layout
Investigated VyOS 2026.04 dns-forwarding config schema (PowerDNS Recursor backend) via templates and conf_mode script/smoke tests

Configured node1: service dns forwarding listen-address 10.100.11.10, allow-from 10.100.11.0/24, name-server 1.1.1.1 and 9.9.9.9, authoritative-domain inventory.internal records a @ address 10.100.11.11 ttl 300; committed and saved
Verified node1 resolves inventory.internal to node2's IP and forwards other queries upstream
Configured node2 and node3 via nmcli to use 10.100.11.10 as DNS server with ipv4.ignore-auto-dns=yes, reapplied connection
Verified end-to-end resolution from node2 and node3 for both inventory.internal and external domains
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service/data health baseline on all three nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 using native /sbin/reboot, backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled each node until exec connectivity returned and confirmed changed boot_id post-restart
Re-verified pdns-recursor service state and DNS resolution functionality on node1 after its restart, and resolver config/resolution on node2 and node3 after their restarts

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as authoritative+forwarding DNS resolver on shared network
evidence.summary: DNS forwarding configured and committed on node1; pdns_recursor listening on 10.100.11.10:53 with zone file for inventory.internal; dig confirms both authoritative answer (10.100.11.11) and upstream forwarding (google.com) work

evidence.requirement: inventory.internal resolves to node2's address on the shared network
evidence.summary: dig/getent from node1, node2, and node3 all resolve inventory.internal to 10.100.11.11 (node2's private IP)

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to resolve through node1, with upstream forwarding still working
evidence.summary: nmcli set resolv.conf nameserver to 10.100.11.10 on both nodes; getent confirms both internal (inventory.internal) and external (google.com) name resolution succeed via node1

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered service/data
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id ebd78841... and active pdns-recursor captured; reboot acknowledged and backgrounded; post-restart boot_id bad09383... proves restart; pdns-recursor active again with inventory.internal and upstream resolution both working

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered resolver config
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id c207ab79... and resolv.conf/getent captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id ce84b78f... proves restart; resolv.conf persisted pointing at 10.100.11.10 and both internal/external resolution work

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered resolver config
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d6298ced... and resolv.conf/getent captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 92f673f7... proves restart; resolv.conf persisted pointing at 10.100.11.10 and both internal/external resolution work
